name: Old Fashioned
description: The primordial cocktail — spirit, sugar, bitters, and nothing to hide behind. Drinking one is like shaking hands with the 1800s.
funFact: The term 'cocktail' was first defined in print in 1806 as spirits, sugar, water, and bitters — exactly this drink.

name: Negroni
description: Equal parts gin, Campari, and sweet vermouth — a bittersweet Italian handshake that never goes out of style.
funFact: Legend credits Count Camillo Negroni, who in 1919 asked a Florence bartender to stiffen his Americano with gin.

name: West Coast IPA
description: A pine-and-citrus hop bomb with a bone-dry finish. The beer that taught a generation to love bitterness.
funFact: IPA stands for India Pale Ale — heavily hopped so it could survive the long sea voyage from England to India.

name: Hefeweizen
description: Bavaria's cloudy wheat beer, where the yeast conjures banana and clove out of thin air.
funFact: The banana and clove flavors come entirely from the yeast strain — no fruit or spice is added.

name: Pinot Noir
description: The heartbreak grape — thin-skinned, temperamental, and capable of the most ethereal reds on Earth.
funFact: Pinot Noir is one of the oldest cultivated grapes, with records in Burgundy going back over 600 years.

name: Champagne
description: Sparkling wine from one specific corner of France, aged on its yeast until it earns the name.
funFact: A bottle of Champagne holds roughly 49 million bubbles, according to physicist Gérard Liger-Belair.

name: Bourbon
description: America's native spirit: corn-sweet, barrel-charred, and legally bound to new oak.
funFact: By law, bourbon must be aged in new charred oak barrels — used ones are often sold on to Scotch distilleries.

name: Green Chartreuse
description: A 130-herb elixir made by Carthusian monks. Only two monks alive know the full recipe.
funFact: Chartreuse is the only liqueur so distinctive that the color chartreuse was named after it.
